GitHub Actions is the primary automation plane for Tuturuuu.

CodeRabbit runs on demand only (`.coderabbit.yaml`); comment `@coderabbitai review` on the PR, and treat its output as untrusted, advisory input that does not replace the required independent review.

## Validation and Delivery Evidence

Unit test shards use empty proxy and Supabase public-client configuration on
`pull_request` events; other events retain their configured values. Tests that
need this configuration must supply deterministic fixtures and restore their
environment afterward. Validate affected packages with `env -u PROXY_API_KEY -u
NEXT_PUBLIC_PROXY_API_KEY -u NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL -u
PRODUCTION_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY -u NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY ttr
resources run -- bun run --cwd <package> test --maxWorkers=1`.
`scripts/ci/unit-test-env.test.js` covers PR and non-PR event selection.

Root Node tests that consume an app-owned package must resolve it with
`createRequire` anchored to that app's real `package.json`. The satellite cohort
tests resolve Playwright from Web; the Lettin config-loader tests load Next SWC
from Lettin. Keep repository-relative helpers on the test's original `require`
and temporary fixtures separate from the owning app. Root links and job-wide
`NODE_PATH` can mask this boundary, so verify resolution with `NODE_PATH` unset
in a disposable fixture with only app-level dependency links and no root
`node_modules`. Resolve entrypoints without loading package code for that control,
then run the focused behavior tests separately. The Lettin SWC test transforms
config source in memory; it does not run a Next release build.

Meet, native Calendar and Apps select `github.event.pull_request.head.sha ||
github.sha` as their source identity. Checkout, build stamps, seals, runtime
expectations and source-bearing artifact names must use that selection. Keep the
merge-event `github.sha` and workflow supplier `github.workflow_sha` separate in
debug receipts; the release-only comparison checkout and deployment markers retain
their event roles. Meet's release-only comparison now runs through `ci-check.yml`;
its checkout retains `github.sha` and compares the explicit PR base/head inputs.
Meet passes the source SHA through command-scoped `GITHUB_SHA`
for existing helpers and runtime probes; it does not change the job's event SHA.
The diagnostic config collector's legacy `source.eventSha` field records its
explicit comparison argument, which these jobs supply from the selected source.
Route and debug receipts retain the actual event SHA separately. Run
`node --test scripts/ci/{meet,calendar,apps}-native-source-identity.test.js` for
source/event/supplier mismatch controls using shell fixtures and command sinks.
These tests exercise workflow wiring without running a build or Worker; hosted
exact-source CI and admitted runtime acceptance remain separate evidence.

`mail-calendar-tasks-builds.yaml` checks out the exact PR head or push SHA.
Its Mail, Tasks and affected Web builds retain real app-build evidence. Calendar
uses a separate native job on Bun 1.4.4 and Node 24.22.0: build shared dependencies,
run owning Calendar/Web/Tasks UI tests, build with the official Void plugin,
discover `.wrangler/deploy/config.json`, then generate emitted `CloudflareEnv` bindings in fresh runner scratch because Wrangler rejects the handwritten stub.
Only successful, regular, nonempty, nonsymlink output replaces stable `cloudflare-env.d.ts`; own scratch is cleaned on success/failure.
Then type-check Calendar plus affected Web/Tasks consumers. Tasks has no owning test script; shared tests do not establish a Tasks app suite.
Root lint and the existing affected-app workflows remain required exact-head gates.

The Calendar pointer requires `configPath` and empty `auxiliaryWorkers`. `scripts/ci/calendar-native-artifact.mjs`
rejects escaping/symlink paths, legacy output, unexpected resources/hooks, private environment files and client
canaries. Live qualification checks exact defaults and materialized input against pinned supplier/parser profiles. The
seal retains that input relationship as historical metadata; restore never opens or rebases the old absolute path.
Retained-state provenance stays unknown; raw config bytes stay unchanged.

Calendar's finite inventory hashes the emitted `client/.assetsignore` and
`server/.vite/manifest.json`, including the hidden directory entry. The ignore
file must contain exactly `wrangler.json\n.dev.vars\n`; Vite records have closed,
typed fields and references to existing emitted files/records. Source identifiers
in metadata are never opened. Credential files (including `.dev.vars`), links,
unknown hidden entries and extra ignore values fail admission. The producer seal,
original/copy checks and finalization use this same Calendar inventory. Only the
SDK-owned `server/.wrangler` directory is excluded during copy finalization.
The shared helper selects it only for the explicit Calendar profile; its default
hidden-entry rejection is unchanged. Test the actual sealed artifact statically
before SDK execution; a successful inventory is not Worker or restore acceptance.

The seal binds SHA, emitted main/config, all `dist` bytes, pointer and generated declarations. The second job restores
without rebuilding and checks the seal before/after dry-run/runtime. Both jobs run `node --test
scripts/ci/calendar-native-worker.runtime.mjs` and, from Calendar, `node --test
src/runtime/offline-artifact.runtime.mjs`. Artifact suites stay outside source-only discovery. Boundary regressions:
`scripts/ci/calendar-native-artifact.test.mjs`, `scripts/ci/calendar-emitted-defaults.test.mjs` and `scripts/ci/calendar-native-typegen.test.mjs` (actual shell step:
fresh output, replacement bytes, failure/invalid-output stub preservation, scratch cleanup and unrelated-file retention). Skips and continued-on-error steps never count as acceptance.

The local Worker suite resolves Wrangler/Miniflare from Calendar's own dependency
links, uses the discovered emitted main/config and denies outbound network calls.
It checks public EN/VI completion HTML, emitted hydration assets and the exact
`/serwist/sw.js` root scope. Tokenless GET/HEAD completion requests exercise the existing
public verifier page through Calendar's auth proxy and native locale resolver;
no actor or workspace data is loaded by its page model. A present token parameter
retains shared verification redirects, so supplying a fixture token cannot replace
this SSR check. The 200 assertions remain strict; failures report bounded request
and Location paths without query/fragment values. Run
`src/runtime/public-completion.test.ts` for real-proxy/model regressions before
requiring exact-source CI and original/restored Worker acceptance.

Calendar SSR diagnostics keep normal server logs to an allowlisted category, with
at most 16 reports per Worker instance. The isolated fixture enables detailed
sanitized records using its `CALENDAR_SSR_DIAGNOSTICS` binding. Handler failures
are rethrown unchanged; the server error boundary keeps the same fallback/error.
Records contain only allowlisted error names/codes/categories, known function
identifiers and numeric stack locations. Unknown data stays `UNKNOWN`; raw
messages, paths, URLs, environment, credentials and response bodies are excluded.
On HTTP 500 the fixture registers the original status assertion and publishes a
bounded initial record synchronously, before observing any stream work. It
requests at most eight stream reads or 64 KiB before cancelling; a single oversized
chunk is counted truthfully and immediately discarded. Cancellation/read/release
outcomes and pending flags remain explicit. Underlying cancellation stays `UNKNOWN`,
even if the cancel promise settles or the reader lock is released. Neither read nor
cancellation is awaited on the assertion or teardown path. The existing
test abort signal stops further reads and requests cancellation; stalled operations
remain pending with underlying cleanup UNKNOWN. Late rejections are observed.
There is no extra timer, retry, race-based closure claim or relaxed 200 gate.
The exact original status assertion is thrown immediately even if diagnostics fail.

Only after natural child close and stdout/stderr drainage does the parent validate
and persist a source SHA/run/attempt/job-key-bound, exclusive mode-0600 JSON packet.
The job key is the GitHub job identifier; numeric job IDs require the run metadata.
The artifact step receives only the verified sanitized packet's exact step-output
path. It never uploads case roots, raw snapshots or SDK logs. Missing owning errors
remain `UNKNOWN`, even with a captured 500. Tests run through the existing Calendar
artifact suite and owning Vitest discovery; a diagnostic artifact is not runtime
acceptance or proof that another app's 500 has the same cause.

The separate offline suite exercises the emitted
classic worker's static-only caching and entry bound. These checks do not prove
signed-in RPC/navigation/refresh, browser hydration, workspace permissions,
provider callbacks or enabled SQL drain retention. Those need an admitted fixture
and separate exact-artifact acceptance. Config-schema or missing dependency/fixture
failures are blockers to investigate, never permission to substitute legacy output.

Calendar publication is disabled for native source. The existing Vercel workflows
reject a checkout containing `apps/calendar/void.config.ts` before setup or publish;
legacy source and the previous Vercel production deployment retain rollback
ownership. There is no Cloudflare publication job or canonical traffic change.
The source name `tuturuuu-calendar` is a proposal, not an observed account/Worker
binding. Before cutover, the parent must record actual account, existing Worker,
domain, bindings, environment-secret names, callback URLs, immutable Vercel rollback
deployment and rollback procedure; qualify signed-in EN/VI, permissions, offline,
log-drain and provider outcomes; and atomically choose one publisher in the root
registry/planner. Calendar has no Meet immediate/no-staging exception. Do not use
raw Void deploy, create resources, or add a second provider scheduler.

For standalone chat initial-settings qualification, launch the source-owned Vitest entry
directly with verified Node 24.21.0. Require primary exit zero, no signal or timeout,
and the owned group stopped; nine passing assertions cannot override SIGABRT or failure.
The optional process comparison defaults off and never qualifies failure; require the same source/control/run binding, SQL197, Web9, Dart9 and fixture/database
cleanup in a fresh exact-source hosted run. Synthetic ports do not prove runtime.

Focused source-only TypeScript checks must use the source entry corresponding to its package `exports` artifact and retain the repository compiler flags, including `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`. When a package contains both a same-named file and a directory index, mapping the directory can hide missing public exports. Regression tests for shared helpers should import through the shipped entry; the Infrastructure desktop public-entry test covers this boundary. Resolve source fixtures relative to `import.meta.dirname`, so workspace-owned test runs read the same files as root runs. See [employee public-consumer qualification](/build/development-tools/employee-schema-qualification#employee-public-consumer-proof) for same-run schema and lifecycle evidence.

- Keep cross-app integration tests outside a package's `src` directory when its
  type-check project uses `rootDir: "src"`. The users-core tenant-boundary tests
  live in `tests/approvals`; Vitest discovers them separately from the package
  source type check. Its config maps the two web-specific aliases explicitly
  while retaining the package's default `@` alias.
- Run tests from the owning workspace with its actual config, dependencies and
  providers. Root-hoisted packages or aliases can conceal undeclared dependencies
  and invalid test boundaries. If a narrow source-alias fixture is needed, record
  it and retain the owning type/test/build gates; do not substitute built artifacts
  or mock away the production orchestration being verified.
- Record immutable head and tree, commands, results, and workflow/run/job IDs.
  A manual preview workflow may report the workflow branch SHA rather than its
  input: verify the decoded checkout matches the requested head. Predecessor green
  builds do not prove a corrected head. New findings or commits require new gates. `programming-app-builds.yaml` runs nondeployment Next/Turbo builds for Web, Learn, Infrastructure, Mail, Contacts and Tasks on relevant pull requests, including shared dependencies; each app result must name the immutable checked-out head and does not authorize deployment or certify a different parent SHA.
- Develop independent scopes in parallel, each with its own worktree and owner.
  Admit heavy local validation through the shared `ttr resources` FIFO after a
  resource preflight; serialize permitted local installs and tests. Require
  exact-head CI for builds; independent CI builds need not be serialized. One
  integration owner serializes main and production mutations. Other owners continue active work and
  hand off manifests rather than starting competing CI watch loops.
- Use native stacks for dependencies: trunk rules and PR workflow filters apply to
  every layer. Verify each selected head, review, quiet window and CI before merging
  a contiguous prefix; queued is not merged. Check the resulting trunk SHA separately.
  Handle absent stack metadata in automation. For fallback chains, retain ancestry.
  After cascades/retargeting, rerun gates; manual base edits may not trigger CI. Inspect actual runs.
- Ship verified independent scopes in bounded releases. Pin and inspect the exact
  main-to-production range, migrations and mobile path triggers before promotion;
  stop if the range changes. Verify the exact merged-main gates before normal
  authorized `bun git-sync`, then verify production deployment and migration results
  separately. A planner success alone does not prove every downstream deployment.
- For mobile, record source SHA, version/build number, signed upload and processing,
  and tester-group availability. Internal distribution and external beta review
  are separate states; neither proves installation or live UI behavior. Record
  supported read-back or device QA, and state any access or verification limits.

See [stack policy](/build/development-tools/stacked-pull-requests) and
[product decisions](/build/development-tools/documenting#product-decisions-and-regression-evidence).

### Python installer and cache boundaries

Discord workflows pin `astral-sh/setup-uv` to the immutable commit for stable
v10.2.0. Upstream stopped publishing major-only tags in v8, so future upgrades
must verify and pin the full stable release SHA. Keep `uv sync --locked` and
the `apps/discord/uv.lock` cache key together.

Ordinary Python CI retains cache pruning explicitly because setup-uv v9 changed
its default to keep unpruned caches. Modal's deployment is triggered by
`workflow_run` and uses `enable-cache: auto`: setup-uv v10 disables cache access
for that sensitive event to protect against cache poisoning. Manual deployment
can still use the automatic cache policy. Preserve the successful-main-run
condition, exact upstream checkout SHA, and read-only repository permissions
when updating the installer; do not enable caching explicitly for `workflow_run`.

## Workflow Gatekeeping

`ci-check.yml` reads `tuturuuu.ts` and emits `should_run` before real work.
`Test` additionally classifies the complete PR merge-base diff in a `changes` job.
Only Markdown/MDX under `apps/docs` or outside `apps/` and `packages/` can skip
unit/coverage shards and upload. Root script tests run for every admitted PR
and their success is always required by the unit summary, because they validate
documentation links, content and the `AGENTS.md` allocation marker. Executable docs tooling,
assets, workflows, manifests, lockfiles, source, mixed or unknown/empty diffs run; both rename endpoints participate. Push validation and ready-for-ci admission stay intact.
`Unit Tests (24)` and `Run tests and collect coverage` retain successful summaries
for docs-only PRs only after classification succeeds, root script tests succeed
for the unit summary, and the gated shards/upload report `skipped`. Failed,
cancelled, missing or unexpectedly successful heavy results cannot pass as docs
skips. Code changes retain every original failure assertion. Only these two
summary contexts may ever be made required in branch protection or rulesets. A skipped matrix job reports its
unexpanded `(${{ matrix.shard }})` name, so expanded shard contexts must never be
required.
Never use workflow-level path filters for required checks: they can remain pending.
Security, CodeQL, secret scanning, i18n and deployment/release gates are unchanged.
Regression coverage: `node --test scripts/ci/test-docs-only-gate.test.js` plus the
complete root script suite discovered by `scripts/run-script-tests.js`. Summary
contracts execute every applicable assertion step, including classification and
root success; testing only the first step can miss shard failures.
For rollback, use `$tuturuuu-rollout-recovery` from the [Codex plugin](../development-tools/codex-plugin)
and [critical rollout gates](./critical-app-rollout). Audit canonical aliases and API upstreams:
a branch or deployment marker can disagree with the artifact selected by Instant Rollback.

For Vercel deployments, the production planner and platform preview perform
affected-app gating before any install, build, or deploy step starts. They check
the current GitHub event's changed files against Vercel app metadata and
workspace dependency closures from `tuturuuu.ts`. Platform preview performs the
check inside its deploy job so protected `main` pushes create one runner, not a
reusable gate runner followed by a deployment runner.

The changed-file resolver must evaluate the full effective change range:

- Manual `workflow_dispatch` runs bypass affected-app gating when the workflow is
  enabled.
- Vercel production push workflows first look for the latest successful GitHub
  Deployment marker for the same workflow and branch, then diff that marker SHA
  to the current `GITHUB_SHA`.
- If no marker is available, push events use the GitHub event payload's complete
  commit file list instead of falling back to only the latest commit.
- Pull request events diff the PR base SHA to the PR head SHA.
- If the resolver cannot prove the full range, it leaves changed-file state
  unavailable so Vercel gating defaults open.

Affected Vercel rules:

- `apps/<app>/**` runs that app's preview or production Vercel workflow.
- `packages/<package>/**` runs every Vercel app whose transitive `workspace:*`
  dependency closure includes that package.
- Storefront UI modules under
  `packages/ui/src/components/ui/storefront/**` are scoped to their verified
  consumers, Inventory and Storefront, instead of rebuilding every app that
  imports another part of `@tuturuuu/ui`.
- `apps/*/package.json` and `packages/*/package.json` are dependency changes for
  their owning workspaces.
- `bun.lock`, root `package.json`, `turbo.json`, `tuturuuu.ts`, and
  `.github/workflows/ci-check.yml` run every Vercel app workflow.
- A Vercel workflow file change, such as
  `.github/workflows/vercel-preview-calendar.yaml`, runs that specific workflow.
- If changed files cannot be computed, the Vercel gate defaults open.

Production pushes run `.github/workflows/vercel-production.yaml` once. That
planner evaluates Vercel and Cloudflare targets from their individual successful
deployment markers and calls only affected reusable workflows. Cloudflare
targets are Colab, Coordination, Lettin, Meet, and Parley. Meet can select both
Vercel and Cloudflare for the same source change. Automatic deployments stay
attached to the original push SHA
instead of creating `workflow_dispatch` runs. Do not restore per-app `push`
triggers for production; doing so recreates the queued preflight fan-out the
planner replaces. Cloudflare workflows retain their `main` and pull request
validation triggers and can still be manually dispatched for recovery.

Each reusable Vercel production workflow uses a static per-app concurrency prefix
plus the Git ref. Do not derive this key from reusable-workflow caller context: that
can make sibling app jobs share one group, cancel one another, and surface red X
statuses where unselected jobs should be skipped. Enable `cancel-in-progress`
only when the inherited event is a push to `refs/heads/production`; `main`
commits and manual recovery dispatches must not cancel the active deployment.

`bun.lock`-only changes intentionally run all Vercel app deploys because ownership
is ambiguous without a manifest or source path.

### Mail, Calendar and Tasks validation relevance

`mail-calendar-tasks-builds.yaml` keeps the `build (mail)`, `build (tasks)`,
`build (web)`, `calendar-native` and `calendar-artifact-restore` checks. The shared
`ci-check` switchboard emits `affected_jobs` before runner allocation. Each build
runs for its app or transitive workspace dependencies; Calendar qualification
covers Calendar, Web, Tasks and Tasks UI together, plus Infrastructure for the
directly imported mobile-calendar gateway diagnostics, including the original and
restored Worker checks. Validation commands, timeouts and publication holds stay
the same. Skipped checks indicate proven irrelevance, not executed validation.

Skill Markdown under `plugins/tuturuuu/skills` and documentation Markdown/MDX
under `apps/docs` are inert for these app builds. Root/tooling inputs, patches,
shared actions, missing change ranges, unknown or
missing workspace manifests and manual dispatch retain all jobs. Both sides of a
cross-workspace rename participate in the PR/deployment-marker diff. Only an
explicit JSON boolean `false` skips a job; missing outputs retain validation.
A failed configuration job still blocks dependent jobs. Regression coverage:
`node --test scripts/ci/mail-calendar-tasks-affected.test.js`.

### Lockfile relevance for Worker and Vercel app workflows

`bun.lock` used to be a global input for every Cloudflare app workflow, so adding
an unrelated workspace (for example a new tooling package) ran Meet, Parley,
Lettin, Colab, Coordination, Cron Control and Devbox Control validation on every
push. `ci-check` now passes the resolver's base and head SHAs to
`check-workflow-config.ts`, which compares the two lockfiles structurally with
`scripts/ci/lockfile-workspace-delta.ts`. A `bun.lock` change matches a target
only when an affected workspace is in the target's dependency closure, which
includes the workspaces behind its `additionalPaths`.

A change is scoped to a workspace only for its `workspaces` entry, its workspace
link, nested resolutions under it (`@scope/app/dep`), or brand-new top-level
packages that nothing could have resolved before. Root workspace edits,
`overrides` and other top-level settings, any modified or removed third-party
resolution, an unparseable lockfile and a missing base or head keep `bun.lock`
global, so the workflow runs. Skipped checks still report through the existing
`check-ci` gate. Regression coverage:
`node --experimental-strip-types --test scripts/ci/worker-lockfile-relevance.test.mjs`.

The paused `docker-setup-check.yaml` and `rust-backend.yml` workflows trigger
only on their own runtime inputs. Shared manifests, `bun.lock`, root config and
documentation no longer allocate a check runner merely to report a disabled
runtime. Restore the broader triggers when resuming either runtime.

Measure scheduling separately from execution when assessing this optimization:
run-created to job-start includes prerequisite work; job-created to job-start
more closely measures job scheduling. Count incomplete jobs separately and do
not treat cancelled or skipped jobs as zero-duration successful validation.
Cache archive restoration is separate from Turbo task reuse. Compare exact-head
hosted runs before claiming push-to-green savings; removing runner demand does
not promise a particular hosted queue delay.

### Draft PR runner admission

Heavy PR verification defers non-security database contracts, platform builds
and runtime suites until the PR is ready. Heavy-only workflows skip their
`check-ci` call before runner allocation. Mixed workflows retain light lint,
type and translation checks. Security jobs always remain eligible on drafts,
including CodeQL analysis and the security-egress contract and its preflight.
The mobile aggregate skips on drafts and still requires every quality, test and
realtime result on ready PRs.

These workflows listen for `ready_for_review` to run the same checks without a
new commit. `converted_to_draft` supersedes cancellable PR runs and starts
replacement security checks even when the PR becomes a draft. Existing
workflow/PR concurrency identities, pinned rerun isolation and serialized
publication, environment, security-classifier and sandbox-cleanup locks remain
unchanged. Push-only verification keeps its existing behavior.

Draft PRs cannot merge. Before adding a required check, verify that its workflow
reports on every merge-eligible PR. Keep path relevance in the existing
`ci-check` switchboard or trusted security selectors instead of adding trigger
filters that leave a required check pending. Regression coverage:
`scripts/ci/pr-verification-scheduling.test.js` and
`scripts/ci/protected-workflow-concurrency.test.js`. Supersession and draft
admission reduce demand; they do not reserve hosted capacity for production.

### Mobile PR build selection

Ordinary mobile PRs build Android as the portable application smoke. iOS, macOS,
Linux and Windows builds run when their native directory changes. Dependency
manifests, localization configuration, workflow/tooling inputs and unrecognized
paths retain every platform build. Missing or empty changed-file data also runs
all platforms. Matching main pushes retain Android and Linux builds. iOS, macOS
and Windows development builds run nightly at 01:10, 01:30 and 01:50 (GMT+7),
respectively, plus published releases and manual dispatch. Store publication and
production workflows keep their existing triggers and gates.

This is an explicit coverage exception: nightly builds validate the default-branch
head selected for that run, rather than every merged SHA. Release and manual
builds validate their selected snapshots.

Keep all existing PR triggers and named checks. The reusable `ci-check` switchboard
skips the heavy job before runner allocation; do not remove a required-check
trigger. `scripts/ci/mobile-build-selection.ts` owns this policy, and its
`mobile-build-selection.test.js` regression suite exercises portable/native edits,
shared inputs, explicit disable and protected push behavior. Run it with
`node --test scripts/ci/mobile-build-selection.test.js` alongside
`check-workflow-config.test.js` and `runner-efficiency.test.js` after edits.

Compare timestamps from exact run/job inventories before and after rollout.
Runner-minutes removed are projected demand savings; skipped queued work does
not establish a guaranteed reduction in wall-clock merge or production delay.

## Coordination native Worker toolchain

Coordination is a Vite+ workspace using the Cloudflare Vite plugin and the `cf`
CLI. `apps/coordination/cloudflare.config.ts` records the deployment identity
(Worker name, `COORDINATION` Durable Object binding, `CoordinationObject`
export); the build emits a Build Output under `apps/coordination/.cloudflare/output`.
`.github/workflows/coordination-cloudflare.yaml` compares that output with the
recorded identity fixture (`scripts/ci/cf-worker-parity.mjs`), then publishes the
exact artifact with Wrangler using the retained publication profile
`apps/coordination/wrangler.publish.jsonc`, prepared by
`scripts/ci/cf-wrangler-publication.mjs`.
Do not change the Worker name, `CoordinationObject` export, `COORDINATION` binding,
or retained Durable Object migrations during a toolchain migration.

Validation runs the `node:test` lease regression suites (`src/request-body.test.mjs`
and `src/worker.test.mjs`) against source, then `tsc`, lint, and the proactive
contract tests. CI then builds the Worker, repeats `src/worker.test.mjs` against
the built Worker and Durable Object, and checks the prebuilt artifact with
`cf deploy --prebuilt --dry-run` and a credential-free `wrangler deploy --dry-run`
of the publication profile. The production job also captures Worker settings
before and after publication and verifies the coordination token survived. The
fixture injects a disposable server token and uses local Durable Object storage.
It verifies credentials, concurrent acquisition, fencing, replay and expiry
behavior without production requests.

For focused local runtime verification, run `node --test
apps/coordination/src/worker.test.mjs` from the root through `ttr resources run`.
It also works as `bun run test` inside the app. Run builds in CI or on an
authorized verified devbox through the shared resource queue with aggregate
memory, CPU and process caps. Vite+ development uses loopback port 8798 and disables
remote bindings and the inspector by default. Only start it for requested
runtime verification. Node 24 satisfies the pinned Vite+ runtime requirement.
The root Vitest project discovers future TypeScript unit tests separately from
this real Worker fixture; the Node suite stays a mandatory workflow gate.

If temporary transformed modules fail collection or Miniflare reports
`SQLITE_IOERR_WRITE`, check for actual temporary-file write failures before
changing product tests. `df` can show free space while an individual `/tmp`
write fails with `Disk quota exceeded`. A private writable `TMPDIR` under the
owning program directory can isolate direct validation from that failure. Set
`TMPDIR` only in the child payload after resource-broker admission. Do not set it
before `bun validate`: its `os.tmpdir()`-based check queue would move shared state.
Verify the destination quota and retain the original failure before one bounded
validation attempt. Preserve unknown files and active jobs. Thread-pool retries passed focused Vitest suites,
but a private `TMPDIR` was also needed for the observed D1 fixture failure;
neither result establishes a universal runtime cause.

## Pull Request Run Lifecycle

Closing or merging a pull request does not trigger a workflow that cancels its
checks or deletes its caches. Existing workflow concurrency remains responsible
for replacing superseded runs on the same branch. It does not cancel a run merely
because the pull request closed.

Inspect the actual conclusion of each run when reporting validation. A cancelled
run is not a successful check and does not by itself establish a repository
failure. Cache retention continues to follow GitHub Actions retention settings.

### Hosted runner reservation and PR queue pressure

GitHub-hosted runners are reserved for `main`, `production` and release work.
When PR CI fans out across many workflows, production deployments wait behind
it in the same account queue. Concurrency serializes or replaces runs but never
reserves capacity. Keep PR load small:

- Verify PRs primarily with local or remote-fleet runs. An exact-head local
  pass is green evidence under the delivery speed grant; hosted PR CI is a
  backstop, not the primary gate.
- Batch pushes. Push a reviewable head once instead of pushing WIP commits in
  rapid succession. Each push still allocates a `check-ci` runner per workflow,
  even when the newer head immediately supersedes the older one.
- Every `pull_request` and `pull_request_target` workflow uses a PR-scoped
  group with `cancel-in-progress` enabled, except the explicit exceptions in
  `scripts/ci/protected-workflow-concurrency.test.js`. Calendar and Mail
  Cloudflare cancel superseded PR revisions. Running main/manual jobs never
  cancel; an older pending main/manual run is superseded by a newer one.
  Uploads keep their independent, non-cancelling `queue: max` lock inside
  `wave1-native-publish.yaml`.
- Heavy PR workflows are path-filtered. The Cloudflare Source workflows, Mail
  Calendar Tasks builds and Programming app builds exclude `**/*.md` and
  `**/*.mdx` from their PR `paths`. i18n Check and CodeQL use PR `paths-ignore`
  for docs and agent-instruction content. Their `main` push triggers stay
  unchanged, so promotion baselines and CodeQL new-alert comparisons stay
  complete.
- No ruleset or branch protection requires a status check (verify with
  `gh api repos/tutur3u/platform/rulesets`). If a filtered workflow becomes
  required, replace its trigger filter with a job-level `check-ci` skip that
  still reports success. A trigger-filtered required check never reports.

### Consolidated cheap PR checks

`pr-checks.yaml` is the sole PR entrypoint for Biome, i18n, docs/SEO,
migration filenames and timestamps, mobile API mappings, plugin contracts,
branch naming and CI admission. The former workflow files remain reusable;
protected push and manual validation still use their existing entrypoints.
Branch-name and plugin checks no longer create a separate run on each feature
branch push. Plugin checks on protected and generated release branches remain.

One SHA-pinned `dorny/paths-filter` job selects the affected callers. Biome,
i18n and docs retain `ready-for-ci` admission; script-only checks remain ungated.
Workflow/action changes select every category. Locale consumer source changes
select i18n as well as bundle edits and `scripts/run-i18n-check.js`. Docs
selection includes mobile pubspec files, Discord manifests/lockfiles and the
safe-fs helper used by the inventory generator. Biome selects `.editorconfig`
and `.gitignore`; plugin validation includes the Git conventions page.
Migration guard edits select migration checks. Mobile API selection retains the original main-base restriction.
Security Checks and its trusted base-commit scope are separate and unchanged:
there is no path filter or readiness label on its PR trigger.

The **Cheap PR Checks** gate runs with `!cancelled()`, succeeds for irrelevant
path skips and fails for selected caller skips, failures or missing admission.
Branch naming is an independent job, so a bad name fails the aggregate without
hiding selected validation. CI admission stays red until this event and the
live PR both carry `ready-for-ci`.
Existing leaf job display names are retained; reusable calls add caller prefixes
to GitHub check contexts. No current ruleset requires a status check. Before
requiring a leaf in future, use an always-reporting gate or preserve that exact
context on irrelevant paths. Recheck rulesets in the same change window.

Among label events, only adding or removing `ready-for-ci` retriggers the
consolidated validators.
Other `labeled`/`unlabeled` events run only CI admission and its aggregate;
each receives a unique non-cancelling group in both parent and admission callee.
Those runs report **Cheap PR Checks (label event)**, preserving the latest
**Cheap PR Checks** result for full validation on the same SHA. They do not
establish a new validation pass. Unadmitted validation stays
in a separate group and cannot cancel an admitted run. This exception applies
to the consolidated workflow; other heavy workflows retain label-presence
admission until separately migrated.

Every selector pattern has a positive fixture in
`scripts/ci/pr-checks-paths.test.js`, using `picomatch` with `{dot:true}` like
dorny. Keep these fixtures aligned with actual validator inputs, including
non-JavaScript manifests. Security Checks is also locked to the pinned PR base
by a SHA-256 regression. New action pins must resolve to commits, not annotated
tag objects; verify their object type with the owning repository's Git API.

Called workflows inherit `github.workflow` from their caller, so each reusable
workflow's concurrency group includes a distinct file namespace. Biome retains
job-specific validation locks and its separate push-only mutation lock.

See the [pinned workflow inventory](https://github.com/tutur3u/platform/blob/main/.github/pr-ci-inventory.md)
for exact trigger paths, all job names, ruleset mapping and execution samples.
Regression coverage is `scripts/ci/pr-checks.test.js` plus the admission,
permissions, security and protected-concurrency workflow suites. Inventory
estimates describe workflow runs; they do not establish hosted-runner priority,
queue-latency improvement or an org concurrency reservation.

### Label-gated heavy PR CI (`ready-for-ci`)

Heavy PR workflows run their jobs only when the PR carries the `ready-for-ci`
label for every human, bot and fleet actor, including stack layers. This covers
`opened`, `synchronize`, `reopened` and `labeled`. These include Test, Type Check,
Biome, CodeQL, i18n, docs/SEO and coverage,
the per-app and Cloudflare Source builds, mobile builds and database contracts.
`scripts/ci/pr-label-gate.js` is the inventory of record. On an unlabelled PR,
every job is skipped by a job-level `if:`. The checks show as skipped rather
than pending, and no runner is allocated. The gate sits on top-level caller
jobs, including each `check-ci` switchboard call, so a skipped caller never
starts its reusable callee.

- **Add the label only when the PR is ready to merge.** Before that, verify
  locally or on the remote fleet. An exact-head local pass (`bun check:changed`
  plus the focused suites) still counts as green under the speed grant, so a
  PR can merge on that evidence without hosted CI.
- **Trigger CI** with `gh pr edit <number> --add-label ready-for-ci`. The
  `labeled` event starts every heavy workflow immediately.
- **Retrigger.** A new push to a labelled PR (`synchronize`) runs again, and
  PR concurrency cancels the superseded run. To retrigger without a push,
  remove and re-add the label (`gh pr edit <n> --remove-label ready-for-ci`,
  then `--add-label ready-for-ci`). Do not use `gh run rerun` for this: a
  rerun replays its original event, so a run started before the label was
  added is skipped again. Use `gh run rerun` only to retry an admitted run,
  for example after a flaky failure.
- **Other labels on a ready PR rerun independent heavy workflows.** Cheap PR
  Checks runs only admission and its aggregate for unrelated label changes.
  Other heavy workflows check only that the label
  is present, so any later `labeled` event on a labelled PR is a real admitted
  run on the same SHA. It joins the same PR group and supersedes the
  in-progress run. The newest check per name is therefore always genuine
  evidence, never a skipped run masking an earlier red one. Labels added with
  `GITHUB_TOKEN` (such as `security-review-required`) start no run.
- **Masking caveat.** Skipped is not evidence. While a PR carries no
  `ready-for-ci`, every later run skips its heavy jobs. GitHub shows only the
  newest run per check name, so those skipped checks replace earlier results;
  merge tooling such as `watch_pr_ready` counts `SKIPPED` as passing. Once the
  label is removed, the PR has no hosted evidence. Re-add the label for a fresh
  admitted run, or rely on the exact-head local pass.
- **CI Admitted check (`pr-checks.yaml` → `ci-admitted.yaml`, always on).** One small job per PR
  event reads the PR's *current* labels with a read-only token and runs the
  admission script from the base commit. Using the base commit protects the
  *script* from PR edits, but not the workflow file: on `pull_request` the
  workflow YAML comes from the PR. The check is advisory, not a security
  boundary. If the base commit lacks the script, it fails red as "admission
  unverifiable" rather than passing. It is **red** when `ready-for-ci` is
  missing, so skipped heavy checks never read as passing. It is also red when
  the label is present now but was absent from this event's payload (the
  push/label race). Draft and WIP PRs show it red, but it blocks nothing,
  because no ruleset requires checks. Green means this event's heavy runs were
  admitted.
- **Push/label race.** A `synchronize` payload carries the labels present at
  push time. PR runs whose payload lacks the label use a separate
  `-unadmitted` concurrency group (`UNADMITTED_GROUP_SUFFIX`), so a late
  unlabelled push run can never cancel the admitted `labeled` run. Its skipped
  checks can still be the newest shown under the same names. CI Admitted then
  turns red with "re-add" guidance: remove and re-add the label to admit the
  current head. Adding the label only after the PR shows the new head SHA
  avoids the race entirely.
- **Residual ordering false green.** CI Admitted evaluates its own event, and
  GitHub shows the newest run per check name. A green CI Admitted run (for
  example from the `labeled` event) can therefore coexist with a heavy
  workflow whose newest run on the same head is a skipped run from an earlier,
  unlabelled event. Before treating the head as hosted-green, confirm that
  its heavy checks are not skipped. If any are, remove and re-add
  `ready-for-ci`.
- **Why not a per-workflow admission job:** reading current labels in every
  heavy workflow would allocate a hosted job on every unlabelled PR
  push. One admission check per event keeps unlabelled pushes runner-free for
  heavy workflows.
- **Always on for every PR push:** Cheap PR Checks selects Branch Name Check,
  migration checks, Mobile API Mappings and Codex Plugin Check by path without
  readiness admission. Security Checks (gitleaks, dependency review and audit)
  and Security Review Classification keep their separate always-on entrypoints. Paused
  Docker, Rust, TanStack and E2E workflows keep their retained policy.
- **Push admission:** heavy workflows have no feature-branch push trigger.
  Mail/Calendar/Tasks pushes target only `main`; Programming has no push trigger;
  i18n targets `main` and `production`. Keep these protected-ref triggers intact.
  Test, Type Check, Biome, Discord Python CI and the Supabase baseline validated
  every branch
  push. They now push-validate only protected and generated refs, and validate
  feature branches through gated PR events. The `release-please--branches--**`
  selector includes production and release-notes branches. Manual, schedule and
  reusable triggers remain independent of PR labels. Biome's
  auto-format PR and outdated-PR cleanup stay push-only. Its PR comment is
  limited to same-repository PRs.
- `scripts/ci/pr-label-gate.test.js` enforces this. It checks that every heavy
  job is gated for all actors/events, feature pushes cannot bypass admission,
  always-on/paused checks carry no gate, and every PR workflow is classified. It also pins digests of each heavy
  workflow's push, schedule, manual and reusable triggers. When adding a PR
  workflow, classify it there and gate every job with `PR_LABEL_GATE`.

## Authorized CI Queue Cleanup

Manual cancellation requires explicit authorization for the cleanup scope. Start
from a fresh inventory of active run IDs, workflow names, events, repositories,
head branches and SHAs, together with current `main` and `production` refs and
live open PR heads. Pin those current heads before selecting candidates.

Classify protected branches **before** checking whether a branch appears among
merged PR heads. A historical promotion PR can have `main` as its head branch;
that does not make current `main` runs redundant. Never classify `main` or
`production` as merged-PR branches. Preserve every run on the current protected
heads and current open PR heads. Older protected-branch validation runs are
eligible only when the explicit cleanup scope includes superseded runs; deployment,
migration, release and signing work needs its own authorization.

A branch name alone is not cancellation evidence. Confirm each candidate's event,
repository, SHA and current PR state against the authorized scope. Freeze a finite
list of run IDs and recheck protected refs before sending requests; if they moved,
refresh the inventory and remove newly protected candidates. Do not expand the
batch while it is running.

Record a receipt per run with the requested action, API response and observed
status. An accepted cancellation request is not a terminal `cancelled` result.
Use a bounded follow-up read of the selected IDs to distinguish completed runs,
requests still taking effect, conflicts and runs still active. Report remaining
runs without a polling loop or a claim that queue allocation has improved.
Force cancellation requires explicit authorization and must stay within the
remaining eligible IDs from the same finite batch. A one-time cleanup does not
authorize recurring cancellation.

These workflows:

- run with default `contents: read` permissions
- bind deploy jobs to `vercel-preview-<app>` or `vercel-production-<app>`
  GitHub Environments

  `TRUSTED_PREVIEW_DEPLOY_ACTORS` repository variable; `vercel-preview-platform.yaml`
  is the exception and also runs on protected `main` pushes so Supabase staging
  migrations keep their same-SHA prerequisite signal

  install/build/deploy work starts
- call production workflows from the production push planner through
  `workflow_call`; retain `workflow_dispatch` only for deliberate operator reruns
- install Bun with `.github/actions/setup-bun-with-retry`, pinned to the root
  `packageManager` Bun version and retried with exponential backoff
- install dependencies through `scripts/ci/run-with-backoff.sh` so transient Bun
  tarball or cache failures retry after cache cleanup
- build selected shared workspace dependencies before Vercel resolves package exports:
  `@tuturuuu/types`, `@tuturuuu/supabase`, and `@tuturuuu/internal-api`
